scenario_category: a story that changes materially over time (negative case: no material change)
description: A trial proceeds through routine procedural steps with no substantive new developments. Tests whether the model avoids inventing a sense of change when none occurred.

articles.raw_content: The fraud trial of former finance executive Marcus Idelle recessed Friday afternoon after a routine scheduling conference. The judge set the next hearing date for the following Monday. No new testimony or evidence was presented during Friday's brief session.

must_preserve_facts: The trial recessed with no new testimony or evidence presented
A next hearing date was set
must_not_invent: Any verdict or trial outcome (the trial is still ongoing)
A sense of significant development or turning point that did not actually occur
known_ambiguities: This case is a deliberate 'no real change' control: the only new fact is a procedural recess and a new hearing date. A good narrative delta should reflect this directly in its summary (per prompt rule 4: 'if there is no meaningful change, state in summary that the core story remains steady') and should NOT pad out newly_confirmed, changed_claims, or open_questions with invented significance.
validation_notes: Expect unchanged_core to be populated and newly_confirmed/changed_claims/removed_or_no_longer_supported to be empty or minimal. A delta that manufactures dramatic 'changes' from a routine recess would be a quality failure the schema validator cannot catch — only human review (usefulness/invented-claims dimensions) can.
